methods.description: Verify immutable inputs and reproduce the original ten-CD/335-CSD #609 audit into new exclusive destinations; reconcile exact source-member mapping and preserve ambiguity rather than apply last-write order.
methods.software: Python 3.12; shapely==2.1.2; pyproj==3.7.2 in an isolated temporary environment; evidence.immutable Baseline
methods.units: source IDs, rows, bytes, and inherited EPSG:3347 measurements

conclusions.text: All ten assigned CDs and 335 CSD rows reproduce deterministically in two byte-identical runs; the original retained outputs remain unchanged.

The pinned #485 identity assessment associates 84 of 733 geoBoundaries source-member IDs with multiple Atlas locations. The old output selected a last-write scalar; the reproduction leaves those scalar assignments unresolved and records all candidates and historical parent chains. No legal or geographic correctness of any candidate assignment is asserted.
Whether these 84 many-to-many source associations are intended and how they should be represented remains unresolved; a bounded modeling follow-up should precede import.
The inherited legal-boundary sources do not establish that statistical units or source-member links are legally equivalent, and NRCan excludes Indian Settlements and Indian Communities.
